description: Includes bottles, packaging, wrappers, containers, and other synthetic polymer items used in everyday products.
recycle_details: Rinse containers, remove caps/labels if required locally, and place in the dry/recyclable waste bin. Look for the resin code (1-7) on the item - PET (1) and HDPE (2) are widely recyclable.
recommendations: Prefer reusable bottles and bags over single-use plastics. Avoid buying over-packaged products.
suggestions: Start a small collection bin at home for clean plastics and drop them at a nearby recycling center weekly.

description: Newspapers, magazines, office paper, cartons, and cardboard boxes.
recycle_details: Flatten boxes, keep paper dry and free of food residue, and place in the dry/recyclable bin. Avoid recycling paper contaminated with grease or wax.
recommendations: Go digital where possible to reduce paper use, and reuse boxes for storage or shipping before recycling.
suggestions: Shred sensitive documents and compost shredded paper if it's uncoated.

description: Fruit and vegetable peels, leftover food, tea bags, eggshells, and garden waste.
recycle_details: Not recyclable in the traditional sense, but it is compostable. Separate into a wet-waste bin and send to a composting facility or home compost pit.
recommendations: Plan meals to reduce food waste and store food properly to extend its shelf life.
suggestions: Set up a small kitchen compost bin or vermicompost unit to turn scraps into fertilizer for plants.

description: Old phones, chargers, batteries, computers, and other electronic devices or accessories.
recycle_details: Never place in regular trash. Drop off at an authorized e-waste collection center or manufacturer take-back program, since these items contain hazardous materials like lead and mercury.
recommendations: Repair devices when possible instead of replacing them, and donate working electronics.
suggestions: Keep a dedicated box at home for dead batteries and small electronics until you can drop them off safely.

description: Bottles, jars, and other glass containers.
recycle_details: Rinse thoroughly, remove lids, and place in the glass recycling bin. Broken glass should be wrapped safely before disposal.
recommendations: Reuse glass jars for storage instead of discarding them.
suggestions: Buy products in glass packaging over plastic when available, since glass is infinitely recyclable.

description: Aluminum cans, tin cans, foil, and small metal scraps.
recycle_details: Rinse cans, crush if possible to save space, and place in the dry/recyclable bin. Scrap metal can also be sold to local scrap dealers.
recommendations: Choose products in aluminum or metal packaging as they have high recycling value.
suggestions: Collect aluminum foil and cans separately since they can be recycled indefinitely without quality loss.

description: Paints, solvents, pesticides, cleaning chemicals, and medical waste like expired medicines.
recycle_details: Do not mix with household trash. Take to a certified hazardous waste disposal facility or a pharmacy take-back program for medicines.
recommendations: Buy only the quantity you need to avoid leftover hazardous material, and store safely away from children.
suggestions: Check with your local municipality for scheduled hazardous waste collection drives.

description: Old clothes, shoes, and fabric scraps.
recycle_details: Donate wearable clothes, and take damaged textiles to textile recycling bins or drop-off centers where they can be turned into rags or insulation material.
recommendations: Buy fewer, higher-quality garments and repair clothing instead of discarding it.
suggestions: Organize or participate in a clothing swap with friends or community groups.
